questions.question: Explain how director becomes the creative force behind a film by / analyzing the essay by Andrew Sarris.
questions.solution_html:
• “Notes on Auteur theory”- Andrew Sarris - director- primary creative force behind a film
  • Director as auteur (author) of a film - defends auteur theory in three premises - technical
  • competence (master the craft) - distinguishable personality (signature stylistic traits which
  • recurs in works) - interior meaning (the meaning/work generated from the tension between the
  • director’s personality and the material)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: In films like Bicycle Thieves and Rome, Open City, how does Italian / Neorealism portray poverty, resilience, and human dignity?
questions.solution_html:
• Bicycle Thieves by Vittorio de Sica - Social poverty is reflected in the struggle of Antonio
  • Ricci to get back his bicycle - his only means of livelihood - Institutions as pawn shops - post
  • war economic crisis – Rome, Open City – city itself becomes a text of poverty – endurance
  • suffers humiliation but continues the search - collectivity and solidarity - Close shots and

questions.question: How does Schatz’s idea of iconography function as a meaning- / making system in genre films, and what role does its cumulative use across a genre play?
questions.solution_html:
• Iconography arises from the repetition of visual and narrative codes over a series of films
  • establishing a shorthand that audiences understand instantly. Eg. the white hat represents
  • heroism, the black hat evil, and the saloon a realm of moral compromise - a genre's
  • iconography also indicates thematic values - this coding runs deeper than simply aesthetics to
  • include dialogue, music, and even casting.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the influence of Italian Neorealism on Satyajit Ray’s Pather / Panchali. In what ways does the film adapt neorealist principles to an Indian context?
questions.solution_html:
• Pather Panchali - authentic depiction of the daily lives of the poor people in rural Bengal
  • subtle emotions and real life struggles of human beings - influence of Italian neorealism is
  • evident in the rejection of the styles and values of commercial cinema, use of natural locations
  • amateur and non-professional artists, lack of makeup, exaggerated gestures, open ended story.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the socio-economic realities of the Great Depression depicted / . CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• In Modern Times (1936), Charlie Chaplin portrays the Great Depression through satire
  • and symbolism that expose industrial dehumanization and social struggle - opening scene
  • compares factory workers to sheep, showing how labourers were herded and controlled by the
  • system - the Tramp’s breakdown on the assembly line and his being swallowed by the machine
  • - Chaplin illustrates how industrial labour consumes both body and mind - Scenes of stealing
  • to survive, repeated unemployment, and being mistaken for a communist reflect the
  • desperation and political anxiety of the era - film ends with Charlie and the girl walking toward
  • an uncertain future - symbolizing hope, resilience, and human companionship - amid economic
  • despair.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the way Malayalam cinema links women’s identity to domestic / spaces. What does this suggest about gendered boundaries?
questions.solution_html:
• Feminine Mystique, despite the social and cultural advancements social conditioning is that
  • “women are destined to be mothers and wives”- Double enslavement, pressure to outshine in
  • domestic spaces and professional areas - Malayalam film portrays this paradoxical state of
  • women caught between the two.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the relationship between Michel and Patricia in Breathless. / How does their dynamic reflect themes of alienation, freedom, and existential uncertainty?
questions.solution_html:
• In Breathless (1960), Jean-Luc Godard portrays Michel Poiccard and Patricia Franchini as
  • physically close but emotionally distant, reflecting modern alienation - Michel imitates
  • American gangster films, while Patricia’s emotional indecision and fragmented conversations
  • reveal disconnection and confusion - Dialogue often lacks coherence, mirroring disillusioned
  • mindset of the postwar generation - Michel’s amorality and criminal acts blur the line between
  • freedom and rebellion, while Patricia’s foreignness in Paris represents a rootless sense of
  • liberty - their relationship becomes a temporary space of liberation, exposing the instability
  • and uncertainty of love and freedom in an existential world.
questions.final_answer: and uncertainty of love and freedom in an existential world.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the concept of the auteur theory and its central role in the / French New Wave movement.
questions.solution_html:
• Auteur Theory - coined by Andrew Sarris argues that the director is the primary creative
  • force behind a film, shaping it through personal style and thematic consistency - Auteur shows
  • technical competence, personal coherence, and a distinctive worldview across their works
  • idea originated from the French New Wave of the 1950s and 1960s, which rebelled against
  • traditional storytelling and studio dominance - Critics from Cahiers du Cinéma promoted the
  • Politique des auteurs, emphasizing the director’s unique artistic vision over commercial
  • production - Director became viewed as the author of the film, expressing individuality and
  • creativity through cinematic form and narrative.
  • (6 x 5 = 30)
  • ESSAY
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How might Mulvey's call to destroy traditional visual pleasure inform / feminist film making today?
questions.solution_html:
• Laura Mulvey’s “Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema”- Critical study and exposing of the
  • innate nature of reinforcing patriarchal structures through narrative designs in Hollywood
  • cinema by psychoanalytical study methods- ubiquitous “male gaze”, “voyeuristic pleasure” of
  • audience- women as passive objects subjected to the agency of patriarchal power- Feminist
  • film making- avant garde films- counter film narration by critical awareness among audience
  • and materiality of camera- redesign film making by equal distribution of agency of power and
  • perspective.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the artistic significance of French poetic realism in the 1930s.
questions.solution_html:
• French poetic realism - Film movement in France- Lyrical narration blended with realism
  • Stylization, romance, melancholy- Use of symbolism- emotional ambience important than
  • plot- working class worries narrated in a poetic tone- usually the protagonists are unsuccessful

  • France.

questions.question: In what ways does Schatz’s concept of genre evolution from / transparency to self-conscious formalism reflect shifts in cultural attitudes, and how do examples like The Searchers or The Band Wagon illustrate this progression in challenging traditional genre conventions?
questions.solution_html:
• Traditional film genres - straightforward storytelling - reflected dominant social ideologies –
  • met audience expectations - shift to self-conscious formalism - films more aware of their own
  • form and conventions - changing audience pleasure from passive enjoyment to recognizing
  • genre manipulation - John Ford’s The Searchers (1956) subverts the heroic Western - Ethan
  • Edwards as a racist, obsessive anti-hero - film’s moral ambiguity questions the myth of the
  • noble frontier and the clarity of traditional “genres of order”- Vincente Minnelli’s The Band
  • Wagon (1953) parodies its own musical-romantic conventions, using self-awareness to satirize
  • the artifice of show business.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

Discuss how Vittorio De Sica uses non-professional actors, location shooting, and a focus on everyday struggles to create authenticity. How do these techniques enhance the film’s emotional and social impact?
questions.solution_html:
• Italian Neorealism- Post World war film movement in Italy - realistic portrayal of poor and
  • working class – Characteristics: use of non-professional actors - poverty and unemployment
  • as themes - realistic approach to issues - Vittorio de Sica, director of Bicycle Thieves - Two
  • commoners, Lamberto Maggiorani and Enzo Staiola played the main characters- shooting in
  • open spaces (factory, streets of Rome), Non professionals as crowd- tram, stops, buildings
  • natural camera lighting.
